name: Public access token (pk)
description: A public access token has the same three-part dot-delimited shape as a secret token, with the header pk instead of sk. The provider documents public tokens as designed for client-side applications and safe to expose in browsers and apps, so one in client code is not a leaked secret. The sample is synthetic: its payload decodes to a fabricated example object and its signature is a placeholder word run, so Mapbox never issued it.

sources.supports: Public tokens are designed to be used in client-side applications, meaning they can be safely exposed in web browsers, mobile apps and other client environments; all public access tokens start with pk.
A client application should only use a token with public scopes; secret-scope requests should never be exposed to the client.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
